scrutiny.failureCase: Shipping vote learning that makes scoring less accurate, as #96's per-topic model did. docs/IDEA.md makes prismis a prioritized feed for the user and their agents; carve-outs only remove what the user confirmed and measured, and retiring per-topic learning removes the cause of the 81% null share.
Adding a second rule for exclusions beside the evaluator's. evaluator.py:120 owns 'Not Interested -> null' and the design writes into that section instead of inventing a new scoring path.

Measuring slice closeness with search_content's relevance score, which blends similarity (0.80) with priority and source authority (storage.py search_content docstring); a High item would look closer than it is. The radius must be raw vector similarity.

Losing recall by removing learned likes: the 2026-10-15 test put likes-only at 30% null against 35% with no learned preferences on 100 items, a gap inside run-to-run noise (9% of re-scored items flipped between runs); stated as a sacrifice.

Building a second vector index; the design reuses vec_content and the stored item embeddings, and the KNN search_content already runs takes a raw query vector, so a stored item's vector can be the query.

Trusting a carve-out line to stay inside its slice untested. The 2026-10-15 <host> check (81 calls) showed a single with/without comparison cannot separate the line from evaluator variance and that a one-item line carves nothing; the design now counts a hit only on two-run agreement and drops lines that null under half their preview, and measures every proposal on real items before it is shown. Containment of a line named from 2+ downvotes stays unproven until <host> has a second downvote.

Assuming labels resolve to context lines (measured 99.3% on <host>, 7,344 labels) and that stored embeddings are of summary plus synthesis (orchestrator.py analyze_and_store_item), both read this session.

Removing code something still uses. Enumerated with grep: get_learned_preferences (orchestrator, refetch, cli analyze), for_llm_context (analysis.py, API passthrough), ContextAutoUpdater and auto_update_* (__main__.py, config.py, defaults.py, docs/configuration.md, docs/architecture/*), check_context_md and section constants (__main__.py verify), preference_influenced (static/index.html badge reads === true, so old items keep their badge).

A knob where structure could hold it: carveout_radius is a calibration value with one sample behind it, so a config value is the honest shape; 'never written without acceptance' is structural, since only the accept endpoint writes.
The radius constant and the label-resolution heuristic drift as context.md's format or the embedding model changes; the preview and impact numbers show the drift on the next proposal.
A one-way change on unearned confidence: the carveouts table is additive, the removals are a revert, and accepted lines are plain context.md text the user can delete.

Fixing context.md reload for carve-outs only: the startup snapshot also ignores the user's own :context edit until restart (orchestrator.py uses self.config.context; Config read once in __main__.py). Reading per cycle fixes the class for every edit.
Statuses nobody needs: proposed, accepted, rejected, removed are each forced by the decided history and the accept, reject and remove actions.
A third context.md parser: check_context_md walks sections and context_analyzer.py has its own _parse_context_sections; label resolution must use one shared walk, and the analyzer should use it too.
Relying on the model to stay inside the slice; the impact measurement is the gate, and acceptance is required by code.
Letting a model group the slice; grouping is code (shared category plus cosine), and the model only names a group code found.
Restating the Not Interested rule; the design writes into the section and leaves the rule in evaluator.py.
Finding accepted lines in context.md by matching prose; remove deletes the exact line text the row stores, which prismis itself wrote, under its own ### group.
Repairing #96's effects only; the cause, votes credited per topic and fed to the prompt, is removed.
Inferring a carve-out's effect from similarity; impact is measured by re-evaluating real items with the candidate line.

Walking an accept: the preview items keep the priority they were scored with, so the user accepts and still sees them; walking a remove: items the line pushed to null stay null. Accept and remove must re-score the items the carve-out affects.

decisions.question: Accept the carve-out design, after a containment check on <host>?
decisions.answer: Ran the check; it showed the impact measurement could not separate the line from evaluator variance and that a one-item line carves nothing, so the design took a redesign round for both.

decisions.question: Accept the round-3 design and build J1 (retire per-topic learning and the auto-updater, re-read context.md every cycle, one shared context.md parser) first?
decisions.answer: Accept, build J1; J2 (carve-out store, finder, naming, impact, API, accept/reject/remove) and J3 (TUI and web views, spec rewrite) follow as their own work orders, and #96 stays open until J3.

carried.summary: Containment of a carve-out line named from two or more downvotes is unproven until <host> has a second downvote; the first real proposal's measured impact is the first test.
gpt-5.4-nano's scores vary run to run (7 of 20 control items changed level in the 2026-10-15 check); carve-out impact counts only two-run agreement, and the variance itself is not addressed here.
